title: Risk Profiling Questionnaire
description: Typed questionnaire with numeric open-entry liquidity inputs and single-choice risk questions. The numeric amount inputs are captured and reviewable, but they are not yet used in the active allocation path.

questions.text: What is your portfolio value? Please enter the dollar amount you will be investing today. The minimum portfolio value for this questionnaire is $25,000.
questions.help_text: Enter a dollar amount at or above $25,000. You can include a dollar sign and commas, for example: $50,000.

questions.text: What is the dollar amount of any major expense you anticipate needing to withdraw over the next 12 to 24 months?
questions.help_text: This captures known near-term withdrawal pressure from house, education, or lifestyle expenses.

questions.text: What is the dollar amount of your essential monthly expenses?
questions.help_text: This supports the liquidity-need reference calculation, but it is not yet used in the active allocation path.

questions.text: How many months of expenses would you like to have set aside for emergencies?
questions.help_text: This is one of the liquidity-capacity signals from the questionnaire.

questions.text: How would you describe your non-investment income?
questions.help_text: This remains a single-choice stability signal in the current typed questionnaire.

questions.text: What is your time horizon? When do you anticipate needing to withdraw the first major sum from your investment?
questions.help_text: This is a risk-capacity question and can override pure tolerance signals later.

options.label: 10 years or more
options.description: Long horizon (no stock cap in the reference wording).

questions.text: What phase of your investment life would you say you are in?
questions.help_text: This is still a single-choice phase signal in the current implementation.

options.label: Capital accumulation
options.description: The portfolio is still mainly for growth.

options.label: Capital disbursement
options.description: The portfolio is being used more directly for withdrawals.

questions.text: If the stock market dropped 25% tomorrow and stayed there for two years, what would you do?
questions.help_text: This captures one concrete loss-response scenario using the new question set.

options.label: Sell everything to protect what is left
options.description: Exit the position after a major drop.

options.label: Sell a portion and move to a safer investment
Invest more money to take advantage of lower prices

questions.text: How willing are you to accept short-term losses for potential long-term gain?
questions.help_text: This is the direct loss-tolerance willingness question from the new set.

options.label: Willing
options.description: Comfortable with some losses for long-term gain.

options.label: Indifferent
options.description: Neutral on short-term losses versus long-term gain.

options.label: Very unwilling
options.description: Strongly prefers to avoid short-term losses.

questions.text: How knowledgeable are you about financial and investment concepts?
questions.help_text: This remains a direct self-reported knowledge question.

options.label: Not at all knowledgeable
options.description: Very limited familiarity with finance and investing.

questions.text: How long have you been investing?
questions.help_text: This keeps the experience question as a simple time bucket.

questions.text: In the past, when faced with investment losses, what action did you take?
questions.help_text: This is the historical behavior question from the new risk-tolerance section.

options.label: Purchased more
options.description: Added to the investment after prices fell.
